title.zh: 卷369 列傳一百五十六 林则徐 邓廷桢 达洪阿
title.en: Volume 369 Biographies 156: Lin Zexu, Deng Tingzhen, Da Hong A
title.raw: 卷369 列傳一百五十六 林则徐 邓廷桢 达洪阿

sentences.zh: 林則徐 ，字少穆，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu, style name Shaomu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu, styled Shaomu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少警敏，有異才。

translations.literal: In youth he was alert and keen; he possessed extraordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was quick-witted and perceptive, and showed uncommon ability.

sentences.zh: 年二十，舉鄉試。

translations.literal: At age twenty, he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the provincial civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張師誠闢佐幕。

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Shicheng invited him to serve as a staff assistant in his office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Shicheng brought him onto his staff as a secretarial aide.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1811 he passed the palace examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷典江西、雲南鄉試，分校會試。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations of Jiangxi and Yunnan and served on the board for the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to supervise the provincial examinations in Jiangxi and Yunnan and served as an examiner for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，疏論福建閩安副將張寶以海盜投誠，宜示裁抑，以防驕蹇，被嘉納。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Censor and submitted a memorial arguing that Vice-Commander Zhang Bao of Min'an in Fujian, who had surrendered after being a pirate, should be shown restraint and kept in check to guard against arrogance and insubordination; the memorial was well received.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he memorialized that Vice-Commander Zhang Bao of Min'an in Fujian, a former pirate who had submitted to the government, ought to be kept firmly in hand lest he grow arrogant and unruly. The throne approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為杭嘉湖道，修海塘，興水利。

translations.literal: Before long he went out to serve as intendant of the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit, repaired sea dikes, and promoted water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted as intendant of the Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit, where he repaired sea walls and developed irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，聞父病，引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, hearing that his father was ill, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821, on learning that his father was ill, he asked leave on grounds of sickness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二年，起授淮海道，未之任，署浙江鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled and appointed to the Huaihai Circuit, but before taking up the post he served as acting Zhejiang Salt Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and appointed intendant of the Huaihai Circuit, though before assuming that office he served as acting commissioner of salt transport for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 遷江蘇按察使，治獄嚴明。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Judicial Commissioner of Jiangsu and handled legal cases with strict clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made judicial commissioner of Jiangsu, where he tried cases with firm and impartial rigor.

sentences.zh: 四年，大水，署布政使，治賑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year there was a great flood; he served as acting Financial Commissioner and managed relief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824, when severe flooding struck, he acted as financial commissioner and directed famine relief.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，命赴南河修高家堰堤工，事竣回籍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother; he was ordered to go to the Southern Rivers to repair the dike works at Gaojiayan, and when the work was finished he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning for his mother, but was ordered to the Southern Rivers to repair the Gaojiayan embankment. When the project was complete he returned home.

sentences.zh: 六年，命署兩淮鹽政，以未終制辭，服闋，補陝西按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to serve as acting Salt Controller of the Two Huai regions, but he declined because mourning was not yet complete; when mourning ended he was appointed Judicial Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was ordered to act as salt controller for the Two Huai districts, but declined because he was still in mourning. After the mourning period he was appointed judicial commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 遷江寧布政使，父憂歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Financial Commissioner of Jiangning, then returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangning, then went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十年，補湖北布政使，調河南，又調江寧。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Hubei, transferred to Henan, and then transferred again to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1830 he was appointed financial commissioner of Hubei, then transferred to Henan and afterward to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Eastern River Conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831 he was promoted to governor-general of the Eastern River conservancy.

sentences.zh: 疏陳稭料為河工第一弊藪，親赴各廳察驗；

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that straw materials were the foremost source of corruption in river works, and he personally went to each office to inspect and verify;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that straw supplies were the greatest source of abuse in river engineering and personally inspected every office involved;

sentences.zh: 又言碎石實足為埽工之輔，應隨宜施用。

translations.literal: he also said that crushed stone could truly serve as an auxiliary to revetment works and should be applied as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: he also argued that crushed stone could usefully supplement revetment work and ought to be deployed wherever appropriate.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to be Governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he was transferred to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 吳中洊飢，奏免逋賦，籌撫卹。

translations.literal: Wu suffered repeated famine; he memorialized to remit overdue taxes and organized relief and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Wu region again and again, he memorialized for remission of back taxes and organized relief and compensation.

sentences.zh: 前在籓司任，議定賑務章程，行之有效，至是仍其法，宿弊一清。

translations.literal: While previously serving as provincial treasurer he had drawn up regulations for relief work that proved effective; now he continued that method, and long-standing abuses were entirely cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: During an earlier term as provincial treasurer he had drafted relief regulations that worked well, and he now applied the same methods again, clearing away entrenched abuses at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 賑竣，乃籌積穀備荒。

translations.literal: When relief was finished, he then planned grain reserves against famine.
translations.idiomatic: Once relief was complete, he set about building up grain reserves against future dearth.

sentences.zh: 清釐交代，盡結京控諸獄。

translations.literal: He cleared up handovers of office and settled all cases of appeals lodged in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He straightened out administrative transitions and cleared the backlog of cases appealed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 考覈屬吏，疏言：「察吏莫先於自察，必將各屬大小政務，逐一求盡於心，然後能以驗群吏之盡心與否。

translations.literal: In evaluating subordinate officials he submitted a memorial saying: 'There is no inspecting officials better than first inspecting oneself; one must thoroughly understand in one's heart each major and minor administrative matter under one's jurisdiction, and only then can one test whether the officials under one are doing their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When reviewing subordinate officials he memorialized: 'The best way to judge officials is to begin by judging oneself. One must master every major and minor affair under one's jurisdiction before one can tell whether one's subordinates are truly doing their duty.

sentences.zh: 如大吏之心先未貫徹，何從察其情偽？

translations.literal: If the mind of the superior official is not first fully penetrated, how can one investigate their truth and falsity?'
translations.idiomatic: If a senior official has not first mastered the work himself, how can he discern sincerity from pretense?'

sentences.zh: 臣惟持此不敢不盡之心，事事與僚屬求實際。

translations.literal: Your servant holds this mind that dares not fail to do his utmost and in every matter seeks practical results together with his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: I hold myself to this standard of undivided effort and pursue practical results in every matter together with my colleagues.'

sentences.zh: 」詔嘉之，勉以力行。

translations.literal: ' The edict praised this and exhorted him to put it forcefully into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended him and urged him to carry the principle through in action.

sentences.zh: 先是總督陶澍奏濬三江，則徐方為臬司，綜理其事，旋以憂去。

translations.literal: Previously Governor-General Tao Shu had memorialized to dredge the Three Rivers; Lin was then judicial commissioner and managed the affair in general, but soon left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Governor-General Tao Shu had proposed dredging the Three Rivers. Lin, then serving as judicial commissioner, had overseen the project, but soon left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 至是黃浦、吳淞工已竣，則徐力任未竟者，劉河工最要，撥帑十六萬五千有奇，白茆次要，官紳集捐十一萬兩，同時開濬，以工代賑。

translations.literal: By this time the Huangpu and Wusong works were finished; Lin vigorously took on what remained unfinished. The Liu River project was most important: 165,000-odd taels were allocated from the treasury; the Baimao project was secondary, with officials and gentry raising 110,000 taels in donations; both were dredged at the same time, using labor in place of relief.
translations.idiomatic: By then work on the Huangpu and Wusong channels was complete, and Lin took charge of what remained. The Liu River was the priority, funded with more than 165,000 taels from the treasury; the Baimao River was secondary, with officials and local gentry contributing 110,000 taels. Both projects were dredged at once, with labor substituted for direct relief.

sentences.zh: 兩河舊皆通海，易淤，且鑿河工鉅，改為清水長河，與黃埔、吳淞交匯通流。

translations.literal: Both rivers had formerly connected to the sea, silted easily, and required enormous dredging costs; they were changed into long freshwater channels that joined and flowed together with the Huangpu and Wusong.
translations.idiomatic: Both rivers had originally reached the sea, which made them prone to silting and entailed enormous dredging costs. They were therefore converted into long freshwater channels that fed into the Huangpu and Wusong.

sentences.zh: 各於近海修閘建壩，潮汐泥沙不能壅入，內河漲，則由壩洩出歸海。

translations.literal: At each place near the sea sluices and dams were built so that tidal mud and sand could not be blocked in; when the inner rivers rose, water was released through the dams back to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Sluices and dams were built near the coast so that tidal mud and sand could not choke the channels; when the inland rivers swelled, the excess water was discharged through the dams back to the sea.

sentences.zh: 复就原河逢灣取直​​，節省工費三萬餘兩，用濬附近劉河之七浦河，及附近白茆之徐六涇、東西護塘諸河。

translations.literal: Further, where the original rivers bent, straight cuts were made, saving more than 30,000 taels in construction costs, which were used to dredge the Qipu River near the Liu River, and the Xu Liujing, East and West Hutang, and other rivers near Baimao.
translations.idiomatic: Straightening the old river bends saved more than 30,000 taels, which was applied to dredging the Qipu River near the Liu River and the Xu Liujing and East and West Hutang channels near Baimao.

sentences.zh: 又濬丹徒、丹陽運河，寶帶橋泖淀諸工，以次興舉，為吳中數十年之利。

translations.literal: He also dredged the Dantu and Danyang canals, the Baodai Bridge and Maodian works, and other projects undertaken in sequence, bringing decades of benefit to the Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the canals at Dantu and Danyang and the works at Baodai Bridge and Maodian, launching these projects in turn and securing benefits for the Wu region that would last for decades.

sentences.zh: 兩署兩江總督。

translations.literal: He twice served as acting Governor-General of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄歲罹水災，大修堤工，其患遂弭。

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang suffered flood disasters year after year; he undertook major dike works, and the calamity was then abated.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing and Xiang regions had suffered flooding year after year; he launched major dike repairs, and the disaster was finally brought under control.

sentences.zh: 整頓鹽課，以減價敵私無成效，專嚴緝私之禁，銷數大增。

translations.literal: He reorganized the salt tax: lowering prices to compete with smuggling had no effect, so he focused on strictly enforcing the ban on smuggling, and sales increased greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the salt tax. Cutting official prices to undercut smugglers had failed, so he concentrated on enforcing the ban on illicit trade, and legal sales rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 湖南鎮筸兵悍，數肇釁，巡閱撫馭，密薦總兵楊芳，擢為提督，移駐辰州，慎固苗疆屯防。

translations.literal: The troops of Zhenqian in Hunan were fierce and repeatedly provoked disturbances; he toured and inspected, pacified and controlled them, secretly recommended Brigade Commander Yang Fang, promoted him to Provincial Commander, moved his headquarters to Chenzhou, and carefully strengthened the garrison defenses of the Miao frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Zhenqian in Hunan was unruly and had repeatedly stirred up trouble. Lin toured the region, restored discipline, and privately recommended Brigade Commander Yang Fang for promotion to provincial commander with headquarters at Chenzhou, tightening the defenses of the Miao frontier.

sentences.zh: 十八年，鴻臚寺卿黃爵滋請禁鴉片煙，下中外大臣議。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Grand Secretary of the Court of State Ceremonial Huang Juezi requested a ban on opium, and the matter was referred for discussion to ministers at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 Huang Juezi, grand secretary of the Court of State Ceremonial, memorialized for a ban on opium, and the throne ordered ministers throughout the empire to discuss the proposal.

sentences.zh: 則徐請用重典，言：「此禍不除，十年之後，不惟無可籌之餉，且無可用之兵。

translations.literal: Lin requested the use of severe penalties, saying: 'If this calamity is not removed, within ten years there will be not only no revenue that can be raised, but also no troops that can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Lin called for harsh penalties, writing: 'Unless this scourge is uprooted, within ten years the state will lack not only funds to levy, but soldiers fit to fight.

sentences.zh: 」宣宗深韙之，命入覲，召對十九次。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Xuanzong deeply approved this, ordered him to come to audience, and summoned him for nineteen private interviews.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Daoguang Emperor strongly agreed, summoned him to court, and conferred with him privately nineteen times.

sentences.zh: 授欽差大臣，赴廣東查辦，十九年春，至。

translations.literal: He was appointed Imperial Commissioner and sent to Guangdong to investigate and handle the matter; in the spring of the nineteenth year he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed imperial commissioner and sent to Guangdong to conduct the investigation. He arrived there in the spring of 1839.

sentences.zh: 總督鄧廷楨已嚴申禁令，捕拏煙犯，洋商查頓先避回國。

translations.literal: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already strictly proclaimed the prohibition, arrested opium offenders, and the foreign merchant Dent had already fled back to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already tightened enforcement of the ban and arrested opium offenders; the merchant Dent had already fled home.

sentences.zh: 則徐知水師提督關天培忠勇可用，令整兵嚴備。

translations.literal: Lin knew that Naval Commander Guan Tianpei was loyal and brave and could be relied upon; he ordered him to ready the troops and make strict preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Lin judged Naval Commander Guan Tianpei loyal and capable, and ordered him to ready the fleet and tighten defenses.

sentences.zh: 檄諭英國領事義律查繳煙土，驅逐躉船，呈出煙土二萬餘箱，親蒞虎門驗收，焚於海濱，四十餘日始盡。

translations.literal: He issued a proclamation instructing British Consul Elliot to investigate and surrender opium, expel the receiving ships, and present more than 20,000 chests of opium; he personally went to Humen to inspect the receipt, and it was burned on the seashore, taking more than forty days to finish.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered British consul Charles Elliot to surrender all opium and expel the receiving ships. More than 20,000 chests were turned over; Lin personally supervised their receipt at Humen and had them burned on the shore, a process that took more than forty days to complete.

sentences.zh: 請定洋商夾帶鴉片罪名，依化外有犯之例，人即正法，貨物入官，責具甘結。

translations.literal: He requested that the crime of foreign merchants smuggling opium be fixed according to the precedent for offenses by foreigners: the person would be executed immediately, goods confiscated by the state, and a written bond of compliance required.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed fixed penalties for foreign merchants caught smuggling opium: under the law governing foreigners who commit crimes, the offender would be executed, the goods confiscated, and a written pledge of compliance required.

sentences.zh: 他國皆聽命，獨義律枝梧未從。

translations.literal: Other countries all obeyed; only Elliot prevaricated and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants of other nations complied, but Elliot alone stalled and refused.

sentences.zh: 於是閱視沿海砲台，以虎門為第一門戶，橫檔山、武山為第二門戶，大小虎山為第三門戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he inspected the coastal fortifications, taking Humen as the first gateway, Hengdang Mountain and Wushan as the second gateway, and Great and Little Tiger Mountains as the third gateway.
translations.idiomatic: He then inspected the coastal fortifications, treating Humen as the outer gate, Hengdang and Wushan as the second line, and Great and Little Tiger Mountains as the third.

sentences.zh: 海道至橫檔分為二支，右多暗沙，左經武山前，水深，洋船由之出入。

translations.literal: The sea route divided into two branches at Hengdang: the right had many hidden sandbars, while the left passed before Wushan, where the water was deep, and foreign ships entered and exited by it.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengdang the channel split in two: the right branch was riddled with hidden shoals, while the left, passing Wushan, was deep enough for foreign ships to use.

sentences.zh: 關天培創議於此設木排鐵練二重，又增築虎門之河角砲台，英國商船後至者不敢入。

translations.literal: Guan Tianpei originated the proposal to set up double layers of chained floating barriers here, and also added the Hejiao fort at Humen; later-arriving British merchant ships did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Tianpei proposed installing two layers of chained timber booms there and building the Hejiao battery at Humen. British merchant ships that arrived afterward did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 義律請令赴澳門載貨，冀囤煙私販，嚴斥拒之，潛泊尖沙嘴外洋。

translations.literal: Elliot requested permission to go to Macao to load cargo, hoping to hoard opium for private sale; Lin sternly rejected this, and Elliot secretly anchored in the outer waters off Chunshui Tsui.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot asked to be allowed to load cargo at Macao, evidently intending to stockpile opium for illicit sale. Lin refused him sharply, and Elliot lay at anchor secretly off Chunshui Tsui.

sentences.zh: 會有英人毆斃華民，抗不交犯，遂斷其食物，撤買辦、工人以困之。

translations.literal: It happened that a Briton beat a Chinese man to death and refused to surrender the offender; Lin therefore cut off their food supplies and withdrew purchasing agents and laborers to press them.
translations.idiomatic: When a British subject beat a Chinese man to death and refused to surrender the culprit, Lin cut off their supplies and withdrew purchasing agents and workers to isolate them.

sentences.zh: 七月，義律藉索食為名，以貨船載兵犯九龍山砲台，參將賴恩爵擊走之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Elliot, under the pretext of seeking food, used merchant ships to carry troops and attacked the Kowloon Hill battery; Assistant Commander Lai Enjue drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Elliot, claiming he needed provisions, sent merchant ships carrying troops against the Kowloon Hill battery. Assistant Commander Lai Enjue repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，帝喜悅，報曰：「既有此舉，不可再示柔弱。

translations.literal: When the memorial was received, the Emperor was pleased and replied: 'Since this action has been taken, weakness must not be shown again.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin's report reached the throne, the emperor was pleased and replied: 'Now that this stand has been taken, you must not show weakness again.

sentences.zh: 不患卿等孟浪，但戒卿等畏葸。

translations.literal: I do not worry that you are rash, but only warn you against timidity.'
translations.idiomatic: I am not afraid you will be too bold; I warn you only against being timid.'

sentences.zh: 」御史步際桐言出結徒虛文，則徐以彼國重然諾，不肯出結，愈不能不向索取，持之益堅。

translations.literal: ' Censor Bu Jitong said that requiring written bonds was empty formality; Lin argued that since that country valued keeping promises, their refusal to give bonds made it all the more necessary to demand them, and he held his position more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Bu Jitong argued that demanding written pledges was mere empty form. Lin replied that since the British prized their word, their refusal to sign made the demand all the more necessary, and he held his ground more firmly.

sentences.zh: 尋義律浼澳門洋酋轉圜，原令載煙之船回國，貨船聽官查驗。

translations.literal: Soon Elliot asked the foreign chief at Macao to mediate; he originally ordered the opium-carrying ships to return home, while cargo ships were to submit to official inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot soon asked the foreign chief at Macao to mediate, agreeing that opium ships would return home while cargo vessels would submit to official inspection.

sentences.zh: 九月，商船已具結進口，義律遣兵船阻之，開砲來攻，關天培率游擊麥廷章奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month merchant ships had already signed bonds and entered port; Elliot sent warships to block them, opened fire and attacked, and Guan Tianpei led Battalion Commander Mai Tingzhang in a fierce counterattack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month merchant ships that had signed bonds were entering port when Elliot sent warships to block them and opened fire. Guan Tianpei, with Battalion Commander Mai Tingzhang, fought back vigorously and routed them.

sentences.zh: 十月，又犯虎門官湧，官軍分五路進攻，六戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they again attacked Guanyong at Humen; the government forces advanced in five columns and won victory in six engagements.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the British attacked Guanyong at Humen again. Government forces advanced in five columns and won six successive engagements.

sentences.zh: 詔停止貿易，宣示罪狀，飭福建、浙江、江蘇嚴防海口。

translations.literal: An edict halted trade, proclaimed their offenses, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to strictly guard their sea ports.
translations.idiomatic: An edict halted trade with Britain, published a list of its offenses, and ordered Fujian, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu to tighten coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 先已授則徐兩江總督，至是調補兩廣。

translations.literal: Lin had already been appointed Governor-General of the Two Jiangs; now he was transferred to fill the Two Guang posts.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had already been appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs; he was now transferred to the Two Guang.

sentences.zh: 府尹曾望顏請罷各國通商，禁漁船出洋。

translations.literal: Prefect Zeng Wangyan requested that trade with all countries be stopped and fishing boats forbidden to go to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zeng Wangyan proposed cutting off trade with all nations and banning fishing boats from going to sea.

sentences.zh: 則徐疏言：「自斷英國貿易，他國喜，此盈彼絀，正可以夷制夷。

translations.literal: Lin submitted a memorial saying: 'Since trade with Britain has been cut off, other countries are pleased; where one gains, the other loses—this is exactly how barbarians may be used to control barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Lin memorialized: 'Since we have cut off trade with Britain, the other nations are pleased. One side gains what the other loses—this is precisely the moment to play foreign powers against one another.

sentences.zh: 如概與之絕，轉恐聯爲一氣。

translations.literal: If we cut off relations with all of them indiscriminately, I fear they may instead unite as one force.
translations.idiomatic: If we break with them all indiscriminately, we may drive them to unite against us.

sentences.zh: 粵民以海為生，概禁出洋，其勢不可終日。

translations.literal: The people of Guangdong live by the sea; to forbid going to sea altogether is a policy that cannot last a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangdong live from the sea; a total ban on going to sea could not be sustained for long.

sentences.zh: 」時英船寄椗外洋，以利誘奸民接濟銷菸。

translations.literal: ' At this time British ships lay at anchor in the outer waters off Lintin, using profit to entice traitorous locals to supply them and sell opium.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile British ships lay at anchor off Lintin, using profit to lure local collaborators into supplying them and selling opium.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，令關天培密裝砲械，僱漁船疍戶出洋設伏，候夜順風縱火，焚毀附夷匪船，接濟始斷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he ordered Guan Tianpei secretly to equip cannon and arms, hire fishing boats and Tanka boat people to go to sea and set an ambush, wait for a favorable night wind to set fire, burn and destroy the traitorous boats attached to the foreigners, and only then was supply cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1840 he ordered Guan Tianpei to secretly arm boats, hire fishing vessels and Tanka boatmen for an ambush at sea, and on a favorable night set fire to the collaborators' supply ships. Only then was the illicit traffic cut off.

sentences.zh: 五月，再焚夷船於磨刀洋。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he again burned foreign ships at Modaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he burned more foreign ships at Modaoyang.

sentences.zh: 諜知新來敵船揚帆北鄉，疏請沿海各省戒嚴。

translations.literal: Spies learned that newly arrived enemy ships had set sail northward; he memorialized requesting that coastal provinces be placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that newly arrived enemy ships had sailed north, and he memorialized for coastal provinces to go on alert.

sentences.zh: 又言夷情詭譎，若迳赴天津求通貿易，請優示懷柔，依嘉慶年間成例，將遞詞人由內地送粵。

translations.literal: He also said that foreign temperament was deceitful and treacherous; if they went directly to Tianjin seeking trade, he requested that gentle conciliation be shown and that, following the precedent of the Jiaqing period, the petitioners be escorted overland from the interior to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned that the foreigners were cunning and unpredictable: if they sailed straight to Tianjin to demand trade, he asked that they be treated with deliberate courtesy and, following the Jiaqing precedent, that their envoys be escorted overland to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 六月，英船至廈門，為閩浙總督鄧廷楨所拒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were repelled by Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Deng Tingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were turned back by Governor-General Deng Tingzhen of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 其犯浙者陷定海，掠寧波。

translations.literal: Those that invaded Zhejiang captured Dinghai and plundered Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: Those that struck Zhejiang captured Dinghai and raided Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 則徐上疏自請治罪，密陳兵事不可中止，略曰：「英夷所憾在粵而滋擾於浙，雖變動出於意外，其窮蹙實在意中。

translations.literal: Lin submitted a memorial requesting punishment for himself and secretly stated that military operations must not be halted, saying in summary: 'The grievance of the English barbarians lies in Guangdong, yet they are spreading disturbance in Zhejiang; although the change was unexpected, their desperation was actually within expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Lin memorialized asking to be punished and privately argued that the war must not be stopped. In summary he wrote: 'The British grievance began in Guangdong, yet they are now spreading trouble into Zhejiang. The turn of events may be unexpected, but their desperation is not.

sentences.zh: 惟其虛憍性成，愈窮蹙時，愈欲顯其桀驁，試其恫喝，甚且別生秘計，冀售其奸；

translations.literal: Only because their arrogant and empty nature is ingrained, the more desperate they become the more they wish to display their defiance, test their intimidation, and even devise secret schemes hoping to carry out their treachery;
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance is bred in them; the more cornered they become, the more they wish to show defiance, test our resolve with threats, and even hatch secret schemes to advance their designs;

sentences.zh: 一切不得行，仍必帖耳俯伏。

translations.literal: when none of this succeeds, they will still inevitably submit with bowed ears.
translations.idiomatic: but when none of this succeeds, they will still have to submit in the end.

sentences.zh: 第恐議者以為內地船砲非外夷之敵，與其曠日持久，不如設法羈縻。

translations.literal: I only fear that those in council may think that the ships and cannon of the interior are no match for the foreign barbarians, and that rather than prolong matters day after day, it would be better to devise means of restraint and conciliation.
translations.idiomatic: My fear is that some advisers will say our ships and guns cannot match the foreigners, and that rather than fight a protracted war we should seek to appease them.

sentences.zh: 抑知夷情無厭，得步進步，威不能克，患無已時。

translations.literal: Yet know that barbarian temperament knows no satiety; give them an inch and they take a mile—if authority cannot overcome them, calamity will have no end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the foreigners are insatiable: yield an inch and they take a mile. If force fails to check them, the trouble will never end.

sentences.zh: 他國紛紛效尤，不可不慮。

translations.literal: Other countries will one after another follow suit; this cannot be left unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Other nations will follow their example one after another, and that danger cannot be ignored.'

sentences.zh: 」因請戴罪赴浙，隨營自效。

translations.literal: ' He therefore requested to go to Zhejiang bearing guilt and serve in the camps to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked to go to Zhejiang at his own disgrace and serve with the army there.

sentences.zh: 七月，義律至天津，投書總督琦善，言廣東燒煙之釁，起自則徐及鄧廷楨二人，索價不與，又遭詬逐，故越境呈訴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and sent a letter to Governor Qishan, saying that the provocation of burning opium in Guangdong originated with Lin and Deng Tingzhen; they would not agree to compensation and moreover subjected him to abuse and expulsion, so he crossed the border to lodge his complaint.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and wrote to Governor Qishan, blaming Lin and Deng Tingzhen for the Guangdong opium burning, claiming they had refused compensation and driven him out, and had therefore come north to petition.

sentences.zh: 琦善據以上聞，上意始動。

translations.literal: Qishan reported this upward, and the Emperor's mind began to waver.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan reported this to the throne, and the emperor's resolve began to falter.

sentences.zh: 時英船在粵窺伺，复連敗之蓮花峰下及龍穴洲。

translations.literal: At this time British ships were watching and waiting in Guangdong; he again defeated them in succession below Lianhua Peak and at Longxuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile British ships were lurking off Guangdong, and Lin defeated them again below Lianhua Peak and at Longxuezhou.

sentences.zh: 捷書未上，九月，詔曰：「鴉片流毒內地，特遣林則徐會同鄧廷楨查辦，原期肅清內地，斷絕來源，隨地隨時，妥為辦理。

translations.literal: Before the victory report was submitted, in the ninth month an edict said: 'Opium poisons the interior; Lin Zexu was specially dispatched together with Deng Tingzhen to investigate and handle the matter, originally expecting to purge the interior and cut off the source, handling it properly according to place and time.
translations.idiomatic: Before the victory report reached court, an edict issued in the ninth month declared: 'Opium poisons the empire. Lin Zexu was specially dispatched with Deng Tingzhen to eradicate it at home and cut off its source, handling the matter properly as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 乃自查辦以來，內而奸民犯法不能淨盡，外而興販來源並未斷絕，沿海各省紛紛徵調，糜餉勞師，皆林則徐等辦理不善之所致。

translations.literal: Yet since the investigation began, within, law-breaking traitors have not been entirely eliminated; without, the source of trafficking has not been cut off; coastal provinces have been repeatedly mobilized, wasting funds and exhausting the army—all caused by the poor handling of Lin Zexu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the campaign began, smugglers at home have not been fully suppressed, the source abroad has not been severed, and coastal provinces have been mobilized at great cost in funds and manpower—all because Lin Zexu and his colleagues handled the affair badly.

sentences.zh: 」下則徐等嚴議，飭即來京，以琦善代之。

translations.literal: ' Lin and the others were referred for severe deliberation, ordered to come immediately to the capital, and Qishan was appointed to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and the others were referred for severe punishment, ordered to come at once to the capital, and Qishan was appointed in Lin's place.

sentences.zh: 尋議革職，命仍回廣東備查問差委。

translations.literal: Soon it was decided to dismiss him from office, and he was ordered to return to Guangdong to await investigation and assignment of duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of office and ordered back to Guangdong to await inquiry and further assignment.

sentences.zh: 琦善至，義律要求賠償煙價，廈門、福州開埠通商，上怒，復命備戰。

translations.literal: When Qishan arrived, Elliot demanded compensation for the opium, and the opening of Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade; the Emperor was angered and again ordered preparations for war.
translations.idiomatic: When Qishan arrived, Elliot demanded compensation for the destroyed opium and the opening of Xiamen and Fuzhou to trade. The emperor was enraged and ordered war preparations resumed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，予則徐四品卿銜，赴浙江鎮海協防。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year Lin was granted the rank of fourth-grade Court Officer and sent to Zhejiang to assist in the defense of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1841 Lin was given fourth-rank court officer status and sent to Zhejiang to help defend Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 時琦善雖以擅與香港逮治，和戰仍無定局。

translations.literal: At this time, although Qishan had been arrested and punished for independently ceding Hong Kong, peace and war still had no fixed outcome.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qishan had been arrested for ceding Hong Kong on his own authority, but whether to make peace or continue the war remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔斥則徐在粵不能德威並用，褫卿銜，遣戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict rebuked Lin for failing to combine virtue and authority in Guangdong, stripped him of his Court Officer rank, and sent him into exile at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict rebuked Lin for failing to combine persuasion and force in Guangdong, stripped him of his court rank, and banished him to Yili.

sentences.zh: 會河決開封，中途奉命襄辦塞決，二十二年，工竣，仍赴戍，而浙江、江南師屢敗。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yellow River broke its banks at Kaifeng; en route he was ordered to assist in blocking the breach; in the twenty-second year the work was finished and he still went to exile, while the armies of Zhejiang and Jiangnan suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River burst its banks at Kaifeng, and en route he was ordered to help seal the breach. When the work was finished in 1842 he resumed his journey into exile, even as imperial forces in Zhejiang and Jiangnan suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，和議遂成。

translations.literal: That autumn peace negotiations were concluded.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn peace was concluded.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，新疆興治屯田，將軍布彥泰請以則徐綜其事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year military colonization was undertaken in Xinjiang; General Buyantai requested that Lin oversee the affair in general.
translations.idiomatic: In 1844 colonization projects were launched in Xinjiang, and General Buyantai asked that Lin oversee them.

sentences.zh: 週曆南八城，濬水源，闢溝渠，墾田三萬七千餘頃，請給回民耕種，改屯兵為操防，如議行。

translations.literal: He toured the eight southern cities, dredged water sources, opened canals and ditches, and reclaimed more than 37,000 qing of fields; he requested that these be given to Hui people to cultivate, and that garrison troops be changed to drill-and-defense duty; this was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the eight southern cities, opened water sources, dug canals, and reclaimed more than 37,000 qing of land. He proposed assigning the fields to Hui farmers for cultivation and converting garrison troops to drill-and-defense duty, and the plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，召還，以四五品京堂候補。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled and appointed as a fourth- or fifth-grade capital official awaiting assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he was recalled to serve as a fourth- or fifth-rank capital official awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as acting Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授陝西巡撫，留甘肅，偕布彥泰治叛番，擒其酋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Governor of Shaanxi, remained in Gansu, and together with Buyantai pacified rebellious tribes, capturing their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he was appointed governor of Shaanxi but remained in Gansu, where he and Buyantai suppressed rebellious tribes and captured their leader.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1847 he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雲南漢、回互鬥焚殺，歷十數年。

translations.literal: In Yunnan Han and Hui had mutually fought, burned, and killed for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan, Han and Hui communities had been fighting, burning, and killing one another for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 會保山回民控於京，漢民奪犯，毀官署，拆瀾滄江橋以拒，鎮道不能制。

translations.literal: It happened that Hui people of Baoshan petitioned in the capital; Han people seized the prisoners, destroyed the government offices, and dismantled the Lancang River bridge to resist, and the military and civil officials could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui petitioners from Baoshan appealed in the capital, local Han seized the prisoners, wrecked the yamen, and tore down the Lancang River bridge to block pursuit. The regional officials could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 則徐主止分良莠，不分漢、回。

translations.literal: Lin maintained that one should distinguish only good from bad, not Han from Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lin held that officials should distinguish the good from the bad, not Han from Hui.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，親督師往剿，途中聞彌渡客回滋亂，移兵破其巢，殲匪數百。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he personally led troops to suppress the rebels; en route he heard that guest Hui in Midu were stirring up disorder, shifted his forces to destroy their lair, and killed several hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he personally led an expedition against the rebels. En route he learned that guest Hui in Midu had risen in revolt, diverted his forces to destroy their stronghold, and killed several hundred insurgents.

sentences.zh: 保山民聞風股栗，縛犯迎師，誅其首要，散其脅從，召漢、回父老諭以恩信。

translations.literal: The people of Baoshan trembled at the news, bound up the offenders and welcomed the army, executed the ringleaders, dispersed their coerced followers, and summoned Han and Hui elders to instruct them in grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Baoshan were terrified into submission: they bound up the culprits and welcomed his army, executed the ringleaders, released those who had been coerced, and gathered Han and Hui elders to hear his assurances of clemency.

sentences.zh: 遂搜捕永昌、順寧、雲州、姚州歷年戕官諸重犯，威德震洽，邊境乃安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he searched out and arrested major offenders in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou who over the years had killed officials; his authority and virtue spread in harmony, and the frontier was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then hunted down major offenders in Yongchang, Shunning, Yunzhou, and Yaozhou who had murdered officials over the years. His authority and magnanimity restored calm to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，騰越邊外野夷滋擾，遣兵平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year wild tribes beyond the Tengyue frontier caused repeated disturbances; he dispatched troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 tribes beyond the Tengyue frontier stirred up trouble, and he sent troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，文宗嗣位，疊詔宣召，未至，以廣西逆首洪秀全稔亂，授欽差大臣，督師進剿，並署廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: The following year Emperor Wenzong succeeded to the throne and repeatedly issued edicts summoning him; before he arrived, because the rebel leader Hong Xiuquan in Guangxi had long been in rebellion, he was appointed Imperial Commissioner to lead troops in suppression and also served as acting Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after Emperor Wenzong succeeded to the throne, repeated summons reached him, but before he could arrive Hong Xiuquan had long been in rebellion in Guangxi. Lin was appointed imperial commissioner to lead a punitive expedition and also served as acting governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 行次潮州，病卒。

translations.literal: En route, at Chaozhou, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died at Chaozhou on the march.

sentences.zh: 則徐威惠久著南服，賊聞其出，皆震悚，中道遽歿，天下惜之。

translations.literal: Lin's authority and kindness had long been renowned in the south; when the rebels heard he was coming out, all were shaken with fear, but he died suddenly en route, and the whole realm mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's authority and benevolence had long been famed in the south, and the rebels were terrified when they heard he was coming. His sudden death on the road was mourned throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 遺疏上，優詔賜卹，贈太子太傅，諡文忠。

translations.literal: His final memorial was submitted; a gracious edict granted posthumous honors, conferred the title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and gave the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial reached the throne, the emperor granted generous posthumous honors, made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 雲南、江蘇並祀名宦，陝西請建專祠。

translations.literal: Yunnan and Jiangsu both enshrined him among distinguished officials, and Shaanxi requested a dedicated temple be built.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Jiangsu both enshrined him among eminent local officials, and Shaanxi petitioned for a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 則徐才識過人，而待下虛衷，人樂為用，所蒞治績皆卓越。

translations.literal: Lin's talent and insight surpassed others, yet he treated subordinates with open sincerity; people were glad to serve him, and every office he held produced outstanding results.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's talent and judgment were exceptional, yet he treated subordinates with genuine openness, and men were eager to serve him. Every post he held yielded outstanding results.

sentences.zh: 道光之季，東南困於漕運，宣宗密詢利弊，疏陳補救本原諸策，上畿輔水利議，文宗欲命籌辦而未果。

translations.literal: In the late Daoguang period the southeast was distressed by grain transport; Emperor Xuanzong privately inquired about advantages and disadvantages, and Lin submitted memorials setting forth fundamental remedial policies and presented a plan for water conservancy in the capital region; Emperor Wenzong wished to appoint him to organize it but the plan was not realized.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Daoguang era the southeast was crippled by the grain-transport system. When the emperor privately asked about remedies, Lin memorialized on fundamental reforms and submitted a plan for waterworks in the capital region. Emperor Wenzong intended to put him in charge, but the plan never came to fruition.

sentences.zh: 海疆事起，時以英吉利最強為憂，則徐獨曰：「為中國患者，其俄羅斯乎！

translations.literal: When the maritime crisis arose, the age worried that England was strongest; Lin alone said: 'The one that will afflict China—is it not Russia?'
translations.idiomatic: When trouble on the coast began, most feared Britain above all. Lin alone said: 'The power that will truly threaten China—is it not Russia?'

sentences.zh: 」後其言果驗。

translations.literal: ' Later his words indeed proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Time would prove him right.

sentences.zh: 鄧廷楨 鄧廷楨，字嶰筠，江蘇江寧人。

translations.literal: Deng Tingzhen. Deng Tingzhen, style name Xiejun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tingzhen, styled Xiejun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he passed the palace examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 屢分校鄉、會試，稱得士。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served on boards for provincial and metropolitan examinations and was praised for selecting worthy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as an examiner for provincial and metropolitan examinations and was praised for recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授台灣遺缺知府，浙江巡撫蔣攸銛請留浙，補寧波。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Prefect to fill a vacancy in Taiwan; Governor of Zhejiang Jiang Youqian requested that he remain in Zhejiang and he was appointed to Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: In 1810 he was appointed prefect to fill a vacancy in Taiwan, but Governor Jiang Youqian of Zhejiang asked that he remain in the province, and he was posted to Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補陝西延安府，歷榆林、西安，以善折獄稱。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, served in Yulin and Xi'an, and was known for skill in resolving legal cases.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was assigned to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, later served in Yulin and Xi'an, and won renown for his skill in adjudicating cases.

sentences.zh: 平反韓城、南鄭冤獄，又全同州嫠婦母子，陝民歌頌，傳播京師。

translations.literal: He reversed wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng, and also preserved the lives of a widow and her son in Tongzhou; the people of Shaanxi sang his praises, and the story spread to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He overturned wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng and saved a widow and her son in Tongzhou from injustice. The people of Shaanxi praised him, and word of his deeds reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，超擢湖北按察使，權布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted by special selection to Judicial Commissioner of Hubei and served as acting Financial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1820 he was promoted ahead of schedule to judicial commissioner of Hubei and acted as financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 沿江民田歷年沈沒，而賦額仍在，為民累，悉請免之。

translations.literal: Farmland along the river had been submerged year after year, yet the tax quota remained, burdening the people; he requested that all such taxes be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Farmland along the river had been flooded for years while tax quotas remained unchanged, burdening the people. He memorialized for full remission.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，遷江西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以前在西安失察渭南令故出縣民柳全璧殺人罪，罣誤，奪職。

translations.literal: Because while in Xi'an he had failed to detect that the magistrate of Weinan had improperly released the county man Liu Quanbi from a murder charge, he was implicated in error and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office for having failed, while serving in Xi'an, to detect that the magistrate of Weinan had improperly released a county man named Liu Quanbi from a murder charge.

sentences.zh: 議戍軍台，宣宗知其無私，特免遣戍，予七品銜，發直隸委用。

translations.literal: It was proposed that he be sent to garrison duty; Emperor Xuanzong knew he had no private guilt and specially exempted him from exile, granted him seventh-rank status, and assigned him for service in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Although exile to a garrison post was proposed, Emperor Xuanzong knew he had acted without private motive and specially exempted him from banishment, gave him seventh-rank status, and assigned him to service in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 尋授通永道。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed to the Tongyong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed intendant of the Tongyong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢陝西按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Shaanxi and transferred to Financial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was promoted to judicial commissioner of Shaanxi and then to financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was promoted to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 自嘉慶時，安徽多大獄，鳳、潁兩郡俗尤悍，常以兵定，責繳兵械，私藏尚多。

translations.literal: Since the Jiaqing period Anhui had seen many major cases; the customs of Feng and Ying prefectures were especially fierce, and order was often restored by force; they were ordered to surrender weapons, yet many were still hidden in private hands.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiaqing era Anhui had been plagued by major cases. Feng and Ying prefectures were especially unruly, and troops had often been needed to restore order. Although weapons were ordered surrendered, many remained hidden.

sentences.zh: 廷楨乃立限，責成保長，逾限及私造者置之法。

translations.literal: Deng then set a deadline, held baojia heads responsible, and punished those who exceeded the deadline or manufactured weapons privately.
translations.idiomatic: Deng set a deadline, held baojia heads responsible for compliance, and punished anyone who missed it or manufactured weapons in secret.

sentences.zh: 任吏皆得人，刁悍之風稍戢。

translations.literal: The officials he appointed were all capable men, and the fierce and unruly atmosphere gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed capable officials at every level, and the region's lawless temper gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 舊例，潁州屬三人以上凶器傷人者，極邊煙瘴充軍，僉妻發配。

translations.literal: By old regulation, in cases under Yingzhou where three or more persons wounded others with lethal weapons, the offenders were sent to military exile in the farthest malarial frontier, and their wives were collectively sent into banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Under old regulations, when three or more persons in Yingzhou wounded someone with a lethal weapon, the offenders were exiled to the farthest malarial frontier and their wives were banished with them.

sentences.zh: 廷楨疏言：「悍俗誠宜重懲，婦女顧名節，多自殘求免，或自盡傷生，情在可矜，請停其例。

translations.literal: Deng submitted a memorial saying: 'The fierce custom truly deserves severe punishment, but women, mindful of chastity, often mutilate themselves to seek exemption, or kill themselves and harm their lives; the circumstances deserve compassion—please suspend this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Deng memorialized: 'These violent customs deserve harsh punishment, but women mindful of their reputation often mutilate themselves to avoid banishment, or take their own lives. Their plight deserves compassion, and I ask that this regulation be suspended.'

sentences.zh: 」遇水災，親乘舟勘賑。

translations.literal: ' When flood disasters occurred, he personally boarded a boat to inspect and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck, he personally went out by boat to inspect the damage and direct relief.

sentences.zh: 修復安豐塘、芍陂水門，濬鳳陽沫河，加築堤閘。

translations.literal: He restored the Anfeng Pond and the sluice gates of Quepi, dredged the Mo River in Fengyang, and added dikes and sluices.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Anfeng Pond and the Quepi sluice gates, dredged the Mo River in Fengyang, and strengthened dikes and floodgates.

sentences.zh: 嚴緝捕，屢獲劇盜。

translations.literal: He strictly pursued arrests and repeatedly captured major bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened pursuit of criminals and repeatedly captured major bandits.

sentences.zh: 以獲南河掘堤首犯陳端，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Because he captured Chen Duan, ringleader of the Southern River dike-breach case, an edict commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He won imperial commendation for capturing Chen Duan, ringleader of the Southern River dike-breach conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 治皖十載，政尚安靜，境內大和。

translations.literal: He governed Anhui for ten years; his policy favored quiet governance, and within the province there was great harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Anhui for ten years with a policy of quiet administration, and the province enjoyed broad peace.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guang.

sentences.zh: 鴉片煙方盛行，漏銀出洋為大患。

translations.literal: Opium was then flourishing, and the outflow of silver overseas was a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Opium was then rampant, and the drain of silver abroad had become a grave national problem.

sentences.zh: 十六年，英吉利商人以躉船載煙，廷楨禁止不許進口，猶泊外洋，嚴旨驅逐。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year British merchants used receiving ships to carry opium; Deng forbade import, yet they still anchored in outer waters, and stern edicts ordered their expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 British merchants used receiving ships to store opium offshore. Deng barred import, but the ships remained at anchor in outer waters until stern edicts ordered them driven away.

sentences.zh: 沿海奸民勾結，禁令猝難斷絕。

translations.literal: Traitorous locals along the coast colluded with them, and the prohibition could not be abruptly severed.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal collaborators kept the trade alive, and the ban could not be cut off overnight.

sentences.zh: 廷楨與提督關天培整備海防，迭於大嶼山口、急水洋獲蟹艇，載銀鉅萬，盡數充賞，破獲囤煙私販。

translations.literal: Deng together with Provincial Commander Guan Tianpei prepared coastal defenses, repeatedly at Dayushankou and Jishuiyang captured smuggling boats carrying tens of thousands of taels of silver, confiscated all as reward funds, and broke up stockpiled opium and private trafficking.
translations.idiomatic: Deng and Provincial Commander Guan Tianpei strengthened coastal defenses, repeatedly seizing smuggling boats at Dayushankou and Jishuiyang laden with tens of thousands of taels of silver. The confiscated funds were distributed as rewards, and they broke up opium stockpiles and illicit trafficking rings.

sentences.zh: 十八年，英船載屬番男婦五百餘人赴澳門居住，驅令回國。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year British ships carried more than five hundred dependent natives, men and women, to live at Macao; he drove them to return to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 British ships brought more than five hundred dependent natives, men and women, to settle at Macao. Deng ordered them sent home.

sentences.zh: 詔下禁煙議，疏言：「法行於豪貴，則小民易從；

translations.literal: When the edict on the opium prohibition debate was issued, he submitted a memorial saying: 'If the law is enforced upon the powerful and noble, then common people will easily follow;
translations.idiomatic: When the throne ordered debate on banning opium, he memorialized: 'If the law is enforced first upon the powerful and well connected, ordinary people will follow more easily;

sentences.zh: 令嚴於中土，則外貨自絀。

translations.literal: if the prohibition is strict within the empire, then foreign goods will naturally diminish.'
translations.idiomatic: if the prohibition is strict within China itself, foreign opium will lose its market.'

sentences.zh: 」十九年，林則徐奉命至廣東，廷楨與之同心協力，盡獲躉船積煙，焚之，嚴私販之罪；

translations.literal: ' In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu was ordered to Guangdong; Deng worked with him in full accord, seized all opium stockpiled on receiving ships, burned it, and strictly punished private trafficking;
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong on imperial orders. Deng worked with him in full concert, seized all opium stored on receiving ships and burned it, and imposed severe penalties on smugglers;

sentences.zh: 臨以兵威，屢戰皆捷，事詳則徐傳。

translations.literal: faced them with military force, and won victory in repeated battles—the details are given in Lin's biography.
translations.idiomatic: backed the policy with military force and won repeated victories. The details are given in Lin's biography.

sentences.zh: 奸民因失業，遍騰蜚語。

translations.literal: Traitorous locals, having lost their livelihoods, spread slander everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Smugglers who had lost their livelihood spread malicious rumors everywhere.

sentences.zh: 廷楨疏陳，略曰：「臣緝懲鴉片，三載於茲。

translations.literal: Deng submitted a memorial stating in summary: 'Your servant has pursued and punished opium for three years now.
translations.idiomatic: Deng memorialized in summary: 'I have pursued and punished the opium trade for three years now.

sentences.zh: 豪猾之徒，刑僇逋逃，身家既失，怨讟遂興。

translations.literal: Crafty and powerful men, punished and fleeing, having lost their families and property, then gave rise to resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ruffians, punished and driven into flight, have lost their fortunes and now vent their resentment in slander.

sentences.zh: 查檢為希旨，掩捕為貪功，偵伺為詭謀，推​​鞫為酷罰。

translations.literal: Inspections are called currying favor, secret arrests are called greed for merit, surveillance is called scheming, and interrogation under torture is called cruel punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Inspections are called currying favor; secret arrests, greed for credit; surveillance, conspiracy; and forced confessions, cruel punishment.

sentences.zh: 誣以納賄，目以營私。

translations.literal: They falsely accuse us of taking bribes and label us as seeking private gain.
translations.idiomatic: They accuse us of taking bribes and pursuing private profit.

sentences.zh: 譏建議為急於理財，訾新例為輕於改律，狂悖紛熒，無非為煙匪洩憤。

translations.literal: They mock the proposal as haste to raise revenue, denounce the new regulations as lightly changing the law, and their wild and rebellious clamor is nothing but venting by opium criminals.
translations.idiomatic: They mock the policy as a rush to raise revenue and denounce the new regulations as reckless changes to the law—all of it nothing but the opium traffickers venting their rage.'

sentences.zh: 」詔慰勉之。

translations.literal: ' An edict comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied with words of comfort and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 調兩江、雲貴，皆未赴，閩防方急，遂調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Two Jiangs and to Yunnan-Guizhou, but went to neither; as Fujian's defenses were urgent, he was then transferred to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred first to the Two Jiangs and then to Yunnan-Guizhou, but took neither post. With Fujian's defenses under pressure, he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 購洋砲十四運閩，以閩洋無內港，砲台建於海灘，沙浮不固，奏改為砲墩，囊沙堆築，外護以船。

translations.literal: He purchased fourteen foreign cannon and shipped them to Fujian; because Fujian's coast had no inner harbors and batteries built on the beach rested on shifting sand, he memorialized to change them into gun platforms, piled up with bagged sand and protected on the outside by boats.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased fourteen foreign cannon for Fujian. Because the Fujian coast lacked inner harbors and beach batteries rested on shifting sand, he proposed gun platforms built of sand-filled bags and shielded by boats.

sentences.zh: 募水勇飾商船出洋巡緝。

translations.literal: He recruited naval fighters, fitted out merchant ships, and sent them to sea to patrol and suppress smuggling.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited naval militia, fitted out merchant vessels, and sent them to sea on patrol.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，英船窺廈門，遣提督程恩高等迎敵於梅林澳，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year British ships spied on Xiamen; he dispatched Provincial Commander Cheng En'gao and others to meet the enemy at Meilin Bay and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1840 British ships probed Xiamen. He sent Provincial Commander Cheng En'gao and others to meet them at Meilin Bay and drive them off.

sentences.zh: 奸民勾通出洋運煙，分責水陸師嚴緝，遇即攻擊，迭有殲擒。

translations.literal: Traitorous locals colluded to transport opium to sea; he divided responsibility between naval and land forces for strict pursuit, attacked on sight, and repeatedly killed and captured offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Local collaborators continued to carry opium out to sea. He assigned naval and land forces to pursue them relentlessly, attacking on sight and repeatedly killing or capturing offenders.

sentences.zh: 六月，敵船駛入廈門，求通貿易，阻之，遂開砲，來撲砲台，參將陳勝元、守備陳光福奮擊，斃其前隊數人，發砲傷敵甚眾，乃遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen seeking trade; blocked, they opened fire and came to assault the batteries; Assistant Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought fiercely, killed several in the enemy vanguard, fired cannon and wounded many of the enemy, and they then fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen demanding trade. When refused, they opened fire and assaulted the batteries. Assistant Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought back fiercely, killing several in the enemy vanguard and wounding many more with cannon fire until the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其分犯浙洋者，陷定海，廷楨率師赴剿，行次清風嶺，詔以閩防緊要，止其赴浙，遂駐兵泉州，招募練勇。

translations.literal: Those that separately invaded the Zhejiang coast captured Dinghai; Deng led troops to suppress them, but at Qingfeng Ridge an edict, citing the urgency of Fujian's defenses, stopped his advance to Zhejiang; he then stationed troops at Quanzhou and recruited militia.
translations.idiomatic: Other enemy ships that struck the Zhejiang coast captured Dinghai. Deng marched to suppress them, but at Qingfeng Ridge an edict halted his advance, citing the urgency of Fujian's defenses. He then stationed troops at Quanzhou and recruited militia.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「英船二十餘艘聚泊定海，內地師船恐難驟近，必改造堅大之船，多配砲火，間道而進，方能制勝。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: 'More than twenty British ships are gathered at Dinghai; inland war junks probably cannot quickly approach—they must be rebuilt into stout, large vessels, fitted with many guns and firepower, and advance by indirect routes before victory can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: 'More than twenty British ships are gathered at Dinghai. Our coastal junks probably cannot close with them quickly. We must build stouter, larger vessels, arm them heavily, and advance by indirect routes if we are to prevail.'

sentences.zh: 」 九月，詔以廷楨等在粵辦理不善，轉滋事端，與林則徐同奪職。

translations.literal: ' In the ninth month an edict stated that Deng and others had handled affairs poorly in Guangdong and instead stirred up trouble, and they were dismissed from office together with Lin Zexu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict blamed Deng and his colleagues for mishandling affairs in Guangdong and provoking further trouble. He was dismissed from office together with Lin Zexu.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，琦善撤沿海兵備，虎門失守，复追論廷楨久任兩廣，廢弛營務，與則徐同戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Qishan withdrew coastal defenses, Humen fell, and Deng was again held accountable for long service in the Two Guang and neglect of military affairs, and was exiled to Yili together with Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 Qishan withdrew coastal defenses and Humen fell. Deng was again blamed for lax military administration during his long tenure in the Two Guang and was banished to Yili together with Lin.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，釋還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1843 he was released and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 尋予三品頂戴，授甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted third-rank insignia and appointed Financial Commissioner of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given third-rank insignia and appointed financial commissioner of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 議清查荒地，親往歷勘，由銀州東盡洮、隴，西極酒泉，得田一萬九千四百餘頃，又番貢地一千五百餘頃，寧夏馬廠地歸公一百餘頃，熟地昇科，荒者招墾，詔嘉其勤，复二品頂戴。

translations.literal: When a survey of wasteland was proposed, he personally went to inspect it; from Yinzhou east to the Tao and Long regions and west to Jiuquan, he found 19,400-odd qing of fields, plus 1,500-odd qing of tribute lands of tribes, and more than 100 qing of horse-pasture land in Ningxia returned to the state; cultivated land was brought onto the tax rolls and wasteland was opened for reclamation; an edict praised his diligence and restored his second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When a survey of wasteland was proposed, he inspected the territory in person from Yinzhou east to the Tao and Long regions and west to Jiuquan. He identified more than 19,400 qing of fields, 1,500 qing of tribal tribute land, and more than 100 qing of Ningxia horse-pasture returned to the state. Cultivated land was brought onto the tax rolls and wasteland opened to settlers. The throne praised his diligence and restored his second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢陝西巡撫，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Governor of Shaanxi and served as acting Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1845 he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and acted as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 番匪擾蒙部，遣兵邀擊於硫磺溝，平之。

translations.literal: Tribal bandits disturbed the Mongol territories; he dispatched troops to intercept them at Liuhuang Gully and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When tribal bandits raided the Mongol territories, he sent troops to intercept them at Liuhuang Gully and restored order.

sentences.zh: 尋回任。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to his regular post.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 廷楨治行早為時稱，屢躓屢起，宣宗知之深，故卒用之。

translations.literal: Deng's administrative conduct had long been praised in his time; though he stumbled and rose repeatedly, Emperor Xuanzong understood him deeply and therefore ultimately employed him again.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's record in office had long been admired. Though he fell and rose again more than once, Emperor Xuanzong knew him well and in the end continued to use him.

sentences.zh: 績學好士，幕府多名流，論學不輟。

translations.literal: He was deeply learned and loved scholars; his staff included many eminent men, and he never ceased discussing learning.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar himself, he loved to gather men of learning; his staff included many distinguished figures, and he never stopped discussing scholarship.

sentences.zh: 尤精於音韻之學，所著筆記、詩、詞並行世。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in phonology; his notebooks, poetry, and song lyrics all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially expert in phonology, and his notebooks, poetry, and song lyrics all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子爾恆，亦官至陝西巡撫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Erheng also rose to Governor of Shaanxi and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Erheng also rose to governor of Shaanxi and has a biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 當廷楨之去福建也，逾年，英兵復至，陷廈門，遂窺台灣。

translations.literal: When Deng left Fujian, a year later British troops again arrived, captured Xiamen, and then cast their eyes on Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: After Deng left Fujian, British forces returned the following year, captured Xiamen, and then turned toward Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 總兵達洪阿偕台灣道姚瑩屢卻之。

translations.literal: Brigade Commander Da Hong'a together with Taiwan Circuit Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Da Hong'a and Taiwan Circuit Intendant Yao Ying repeatedly drove them back.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，同獲譴。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, both were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was concluded, both were punished.

sentences.zh: 達洪阿 達洪阿，字厚庵，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Da Hong'a. Da Hong'a, style name Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a, styled Hou'an, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由護軍洊擢總兵。

translations.literal: From a guardsman he was repeatedly promoted to Brigade Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a guardsman, he rose step by step to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年，調台灣鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he was transferred to Taiwan garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was transferred to command the Taiwan garrison.

sentences.zh: 十八年，剿嘉義縣匪沈和等，賜花翎，加提督銜。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he suppressed the bandits Shen He and others in Jiayi County, was granted the peacock feather, and given the rank of Provincial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he suppressed the bandits Shen He and others in Jiayi County, was awarded the peacock feather, and given provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 二十一年八月，英兵船至雞籠海口，達洪阿與姚瑩督兵御之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year British warships reached Jilong Harbor; Da Hong'a and Yao Ying directed troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1841 British warships reached Jilong Harbor. Da Hong'a and Yao Ying directed the defense.

sentences.zh: 副將邱鎮功燃巨砲折其桅，敵船衝礁破碎，擒斬甚眾，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: Vice-Commander Qiu Zhengong fired a great cannon and broke their mast; the enemy ship struck a reef and was shattered, and many were captured and killed; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Commander Qiu Zhengong fired a heavy cannon and snapped the enemy mast. The enemy ship struck a reef and broke apart, and many of the crew were captured or killed. Da Hong'a was awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 九月，敵船再至雞籠三沙灣，复卻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month enemy ships again reached Sansha Bay at Jilong, and he again repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month enemy ships returned to Sansha Bay at Jilong, and he drove them off again.

sentences.zh: 剿平嘉義、鳳山土匪，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: He suppressed bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed bandits in Jiayi and Fengshan and was granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，敵船犯淡水、彰化間之大安港，欲入口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year enemy ships attacked Da'an Harbor between Tamsui and Zhanghua, intending to enter the port.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 enemy ships attacked Da'an Harbor between Tamsui and Zhanghua, intending to force their way in.

sentences.zh: 達洪阿謀於姚瑩，瑩曰：「此未可與海上爭鋒，必以計殲之。

translations.literal: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying; Yao said: 'This is not a case where we can contend at sea; they must be destroyed by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong'a consulted Yao Ying, who said: 'We cannot meet them head-on at sea. They must be destroyed by stratagem.'

sentences.zh: 」乃募漁舟投敵任鄉導，誘令從土地公港入，擱淺中流，伏發，大破之，落水死者無算，其竄入漁舟者，擊斬殆盡。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they recruited fishing boats, sent men to the enemy to serve as guides, lured them to enter by Tudi Gong Harbor, stranded them midstream, sprang an ambush, and routed them greatly; those who drowned were beyond counting, and those who fled into fishing boats were nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: They recruited fishing boats and sent men to pose as guides for the enemy, luring the ships into Tudi Gong Harbor where they ran aground midstream. An ambush was sprung, the enemy was routed, countless men drowned, and those who fled into fishing boats were nearly all killed.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉台灣三次破敵，達洪阿等智勇兼施，大揚國威，賜號阿克達春巴圖魯，加太子太保銜。

translations.literal: An edict praised Taiwan's three defeats of the enemy, stating that Da Hong'a and others combined wisdom and courage and greatly displayed national prestige; he was granted the title Akedachun Baturu and the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended Taiwan's three victories over the enemy, praising Da Hong'a and his colleagues for combining strategy and courage and greatly enhancing national prestige. He was granted the title Akedachun Baturu and the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 敵船遊奕外洋，乘間掩擊，迭有俘獲，遂不復至。

translations.literal: Enemy ships cruised in outer waters; taking opportunities they launched surprise attacks and repeatedly captured prisoners, and the enemy then did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy ships cruised offshore, Da Hong'a struck at every opening, repeatedly taking prisoners, and the enemy did not return.

sentences.zh: 既而英師再陷定海，浙江、江蘇軍屢挫，乃議和。

translations.literal: Soon afterward British forces again captured Dinghai, the armies of Zhejiang and Jiangsu suffered repeated defeats, and peace negotiations were then undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward British forces captured Dinghai again, imperial armies in Zhejiang and Jiangsu suffered repeated defeats, and peace negotiations began.

sentences.zh: 英將濮鼎查訴稱台灣所戮皆遭風難民，達洪阿等冒功捏奏，命總督怡良赴台灣查辦。

translations.literal: British General Pottinger complained that those killed in Taiwan were all shipwrecked victims, that Da Hong'a and others had falsely claimed merit and fabricated memorials, and the order was given for Governor Yiliang to go to Taiwan to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: British general Pottinger claimed that those killed in Taiwan were shipwrecked civilians and that Da Hong'a and his colleagues had fabricated their reports to claim false credit. Governor Yiliang was ordered to Taiwan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 至即傳旨革職逮問，兵民不服，勢洶洶，達洪阿等撫慰乃散。

translations.literal: Upon arrival an edict was immediately transmitted dismissing them from office and ordering arrest for inquiry; soldiers and civilians were discontented and the situation grew turbulent; Da Hong'a and the others pacified them and the crowd then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival an edict immediately dismissed Da Hong'a from office and ordered his arrest. Soldiers and civilians were outraged and the situation grew volatile until Da Hong'a and his colleagues calmed the crowd.

sentences.zh: 至京，下刑部獄，尋釋之，予三等侍衛，充哈密辦事大臣。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he was placed in the Ministry of Justice prison; soon he was released, granted the rank of Third-Class Bodyguard, and appointed Commissioner at Hami.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital he was imprisoned by the Ministry of Justice, but was soon released, given the rank of third-class bodyguard, and appointed commissioner at Hami.

sentences.zh: 歷伊犁參贊大臣，西寧辦事大臣。

translations.literal: He successively served as Assistant Commissioner at Yili and Commissioner at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as assistant commissioner at Yili and commissioner at Xining.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，偕陝甘總督布彥泰剿平黑錯寺番匪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, together with Governor-General Buyantai of Shaanxi and Gansu, he suppressed and pacified the tribal bandits of Heicuosi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846 he joined Governor-General Buyantai of Shaanxi and Gansu in suppressing the tribal insurgents at Heicuosi.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was appointed Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he was appointed vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，從大學士賽尚阿勦賊廣西，破紫金山西南砲台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest battery on Zijin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest battery on Zijin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 以病回京。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪犯畿輔，率八旗兵赴臨洺關進剿。

translations.literal: In the third year Guangdong rebels invaded the capital region; he led Eight Banner troops to Linming Pass to advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, when Guangdong rebels threatened the capital region, he led Eight Banner troops to Linming Pass to attack them.

sentences.zh: 從欽差大臣勝保擊賊靜海，四戰皆捷，追至下西河，副都統佟鑑、天津知縣謝子澄陣亡。

translations.literal: Following Imperial Commissioner Senggelinqin he attacked rebels at Jinghai, won victory in four battles, pursued them to Xiaxihe, and Vice Commander-in-Chief Tong Jian and Tianjin Magistrate Xie Zicheng died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Imperial Commissioner Senggelinqin, he fought rebels at Jinghai, won four successive engagements, and pursued them to Xiaxihe. Vice Commander-in-Chief Tong Jian and Tianjin Magistrate Xie Zicheng were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 詔斥達洪阿先退，革職，留營效力。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Da Hong'a for retreating first, dismissed him from office, and ordered him to remain with the army to redeem himself through service.
